title: Bibimbap
summary: Four seasoned vegetables and a gochujang sauce. Make the vegetables the night before and the morning takes 5 minutes.
intro:
Bibimbap is not a difficult dish, it is a fiddly one. Each seasoned vegetable takes 5 minutes on its own; it is doing four of them at once that feels like a lot.

Gathering up leftover vegetable side dishes is how this food was made in the first place. There is no need to make everything from scratch.

items.name: Korean courgette (aehobak; a young courgette / zucchini works)

steps: Mix all the sauce ingredients together. The 1 Tbsp (15 mL) of water is there to loosen the paste, so adjust it as you watch the consistency.
Blanch the spinach in boiling salted water for 30 seconds, rinse it in cold water, squeeze it dry and dress it with soup soy sauce, garlic and sesame oil.
Cook the soybean sprouts in 200 mL (scant 1 cup) water with salt, covered, for 5 minutes, then dress them with salt, garlic and sesame oil.
Cut the courgette into matchsticks and stir-fry it with a pinch of salt in an oiled pan for 2 minutes.
Cut the carrot into matchsticks and stir-fry it the same way for 2 minutes. You can carry straight on in the same pan without wiping it.
Slice the shiitake thinly and stir-fry for 2 minutes with 1 tsp (5 mL) soy sauce.
If you are using beef, season it with 1 Tbsp (15 mL) soy sauce, 1/2 tsp sugar, garlic and sesame oil, then fry it.
Fry the eggs sunny side up, keeping the yolks runny. A yolk that runs is what makes it mix smoothly.
Put the rice in a bowl and arrange the vegetables around it by colour. Set the egg in the middle and serve the sauce alongside.
tips: The seasoned vegetables can be made the day before and kept in the fridge. Twenty minutes at room temperature before eating brings the sesame oil aroma back.
You do not need a stone bowl. Swirl sesame oil around a deep bowl before adding the rice and you get a similar toasty flavour.
Make a generous batch of the sauce and it keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks. It is also good on noodles or on raw fish over rice (hoedeopbap).
